FP-7 ballistic missile made in Ukraine were deployed for the first time. This is progress, but one should not expect miracles.

“Ukrainian tactical ballistic missile. FP-7. First combat deployment. Thank you for the results. Next step: serial production. Glory to Ukraine!” With these words and a short video, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky announced a long-awaited milestone in Ukraine’s arms programme. The next step is expected to be the deployment of the larger and more dangerous FP-9 missile.

Actual Article Body:
Vladimir Putin ordered his military commanders to abandon the rules of war in airstrikes on Ukraine, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told the Financial Times in an interview. Ukrainian intelligence agencies obtained the information through intercepts, he said.

Lifting those restrictions led to a sharp increase in strikes on civilian targets. Zelensky said Putin gave the order in September, when Russia stepped up its strikes on Kyiv, hitting schools, hospitals, and data centers. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told the newspaper that Russian forces do not strike civilian infrastructure.
